descriptive_title: Grade 3 Mathematics: Demonstrations — Probability and Predictions (D2.1-D2.2)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.D2.1: use mathematical language, including the terms 'impossible', 'unlikely', 'equally likely', 'likely', and 'certain', to describe the likelihood of events happening, and use that likelihood to make predictions and informed decisions
curriculum_expectations.D2.2: make and test predictions about the likelihood that the mean and the mode(s) of a data set will be the same for data collected from different populations

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 3 unit on probability (D2.1-D2.2) framed around 'Likely, Unlikely, Impossible' — Lucky Lou the Loon and Maybe Mae the Cat. Day 1 introduces the FIVE-WORD likelihood scale (impossible, unlikely, equally likely, likely, certain). Day 2 uses the scale to make and explain predictions. Day 3 introduces SECOND-POPULATION testing (compare predictions across two groups). Day 4 introduces predicting MEAN and MODE across populations. Day 5 closes with a Big Predict Capstone integrating both expectations. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will use the 5-word likelihood scale, predict outcomes, test predictions across two populations, and predict whether mean and mode stay the same.

lesson_arc.big_idea: There are FIVE likelihood words: impossible, unlikely, equally likely, likely, certain. They sit on a SCALE.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use all 5 likelihood words on the scale.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Lucky Lou teaches the 5-word scale; children sort 12 events along it.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We use likelihood words to PREDICT and make INFORMED DECISIONS.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use likelihood words to make a prediction.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Maybe Mae predicts coin flips and dice; children predict 6 events.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We test predictions by collecting data from TWO populations and comparing.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can test a prediction by comparing two populations.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Lucky Lou compares Class A and Class B favourites; children test their own.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can predict whether MEAN and MODE will be the SAME or DIFFERENT across populations.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can predict if mean and mode stay the same across two populations.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Maybe Mae predicts mean+mode across two classes; children calculate.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Predictors use the SCALE plus mean and mode to PREDICT, TEST, and DECIDE.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can predict using the scale, then test with mean and mode.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children run a full predict-test cycle: word, predict, collect, compare.

recurring_characters.name: Lucky Lou the Loon
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. Same Lucky Lou from G1/G2 likelihood units; now uses the full 5-word scale. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A cheerful young loon with bright eyes and a clover charm around his neck, holding a 5-word scale chart.

recurring_characters.name: Maybe Mae the Cat
recurring_characters.role: Lucky Lou's partner. Mean+mode prediction character. Cameo Lessons 2-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A small cat in a striped shirt with a question-mark hat, holding a clipboard and calculator.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: Just as likely to happen as not. 50/50.
Probably will happen, but not for sure.
What we think WILL happen, before testing.
A group we collect data from. (Class A, Class B.)
The 'fair share'. Add all values, divide by count.

pedagogical_notes: Grade 3 expands G2 (3-word scale: impossible/possible/certain) to FIVE words by adding 'unlikely' and 'equally likely'.
The scale is visual — left = impossible, right = certain, middle = equally likely.
D2.2 is new — predict and test across two populations.
Mean+mode prediction connects D1.4 (computation) to D2.2 (prediction).
Conclusions use the 5-word scale, not just yes/no.
canadian_context_notes: Examples: snow in July (impossible), maple leaves in fall (certain).
Hockey: predicting a Leafs win (likely or unlikely depending on class poll).
Tim Hortons: rolling Roll-Up cup (unlikely to win).
